newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr on strong demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Tuesday down against the dollar on strong corporate demand for the US currency, dealers said.
They said the rupee ended at 35.825/830 per dollar after opening at 35.78/79, unchanged from Monday's close.
"There was good demand from the State Bank of India and other banks," said a dealer. "It looks like month-end demand hit the market. I think some banks were also covering short positions today."
Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.79 and a low of 35.83 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) did not buy dollars on Tuesday.
RBI buying on Monday pushed the rupee down to an intra-day of 35.80, from opening quotes of 35.745/755, before it retraced to close at 35.78/79.
Dealers said the rupee could weaken further during the week if demand persisted.
"If today's level of dollar demand persists through the next few days, we should see the rupee dipping to at least 35.87/88 by Friday," said a dealer.
Dealers said the rupee moved up marginally against the forward dollar in quiet trade.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Tuesday at 4.64 percent against Monday's close of 4.75 percent.
"There was some demand but this was more than offset by selling from corporates," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"But if the rupee drops further in spot and approaches 35.90, there could be some booking of forward dollars and premiums could rise," the dealer said.
